conviction_note: ZIM is a merger-arb name ($29.69 against Hapag-Lloyd's $35 cash, an 18% spread, because Israel's golden-share approval is unresolved). Its Q3 was largely pre-announced by the 9 Oct guidance raise and a Q3-based dividend is already flagged. The live questions are a second FY raise (Hapag-Lloyd raised again on 11 Nov), the size of the dividend, and deal commentary on the 08:00 ET call. They roughly offset against a reaction function that sold a large beat on 19 Aug 2026 (-6%), while Maersk fell 9-11% on its own raise on 5 Nov. So p_up is 49 on an abs move of 5.5, and the findings sum to -0.4. The two numbers agree in being near zero.
bar: Disputed. Q3 2026 consensus EPS is $4.77 on $2.49bn revenue (Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-11-10, https://finviz.com/news/420723/zims-raised-ebitda-outlook-faces-its-first-real-test-as-street-bets-on-sevenfold-profit-jump). Other sources give $3.85 / $2.537bn (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/ZIM/estimates) and $5.15 / $2.56bn (Benzinga, 30 Oct snapshot, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ZIM/earnings-forecasts). No two sources agree, so every finding is capped small. The company bar is the FY2026 guide raised on 2026-10-09: adjusted EBITDA $2.7-3.0bn and adjusted EBIT $1.4-1.7bn, up from $2.0-2.4bn and $0.7-1.1bn (https://www.foodbusinessmea.com/?p=2164464). With H1 adjusted EBIT of about $164m (Q1 -$5m, Q2 $169m), H2 EBIT must be about $1.24-1.54bn. My own inference, not a sourced number: Q3 EPS of roughly $4.3-6.2 depending on the Q3/Q4 split, which brackets the $4.77 consensus. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on EPS against $4.77 and is a weak lean.
positioning_check: Short interest is low. FINRA showed 3,083,242 shares short at the 2026-09-15 settlement, about 2.6% of shares outstanding, with 2.13 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/zim/short-interest via search snippet; nothing found after mid-September). The 2025 figure of about 18% of float is stale. This is not a crowded short, so there is no squeeze mechanism. Baseline options: front expiry 2026-11-20, ATM IV 64.5%, 25-delta skew +20.4 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.54. But the ATM spread is 81% of mid, so the baseline flags the chain as too wide to mean anything and gives no event-implied move. A rough read of 64.5% IV over 3 days, net of 29.7% realised vol, gives about 6%, which is unreliable. Tape: +5.64% over 5 days, +1.87% over 20 days, 3.9% below the 52-week high, 77% above the 52-week low. The stock is anchored by the $35 cash deal: the spread of about $5.31 (18%) prices substantial risk that the Israeli golden-share approval fails or slips.

findings.finding: Hapag-Lloyd, ZIM's acquirer and a direct peer, raised FY2026 guidance a second time on 2026-11-11: EBITDA to $4.6-5.0bn from $3.9-4.4bn (+16% at the midpoint) and EBIT to $2.0-2.4bn from $1.25-1.75bn. Q3 average freight rates were $1,808/TEU (+23% q/q), and press reads the raise as a stronger-than-expected Q4 (rates held up on congestion and Cape routing). ZIM's own raise (EBITDA $2.7-3.0bn) is dated 2026-10-09, five weeks before Hapag's second raise. Transpacific spot rates (ZIM's core lane) were $7,416/FEU Shanghai-LA on 12 Nov, against $7,185-7,838 through September. That is consistent with Q4 realised rates at or above Q3, so ZIM could raise or narrow its FY range upward on 18 Nov. The market bar for the guide is the 9 Oct range; no preview I found expects a second raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (19 Aug 2026): a large EPS and revenue beat with a new FY guide, and the stock fell about 6% intraday to $26.77 (https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15430207503746048). Peer Maersk raised its guide on 5 Nov 2026 and fell 8.6-11% because the raise was 'largely expected' (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/boxships/maersk-shares-fall-despite-third-profit-guidance-raise-in-2026). Hapag's own stock rose up to 6.8% on its 11 Nov raise (https://finimize.com/content/hapag-lloyd-raised-guidance-again-as-freight-rates-held-up). Mixed: raises have not reliably paid in this sector in this cycle.
findings.why_not_priced: ZIM's consensus ($4.77 EPS, Finviz 10 Nov) and its guide predate Hapag's 11 Nov raise. If the market already expected a second ZIM raise, previews would discuss one, and the stock would sit closer to its $30.98 post-print high or above it. Instead it is at $29.69 and the 10 Nov preview frames the 9 Oct raise as facing 'its first real test'. The deal cap blunts any re-rating: on a $35 cash deal, upside from fundamentals mostly reduces break-risk downside.
findings.independence: The Hapag-Lloyd ad hoc of 28 Sep 2026 (first raise; https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/EQS-Adhoc-Hapag-Lloyd-further-raises-its-earnings-outlook-for-the-current-financial-year-9c1747c6-aaed-4a79-ae28-cd55f24dbe75) and Maersk's third 2026 raise on 5 Nov (https://www.foodbusinessmea.com/?p=2165405) point the same way. The transpacific spot series (Drewry WCI, https://www.shipuniverse.com/?p=27702) is a separate source; the same series also underlies the negative finding on the falling WCI trend. All of this is peer and proxy evidence, not ZIM's own number.

findings.finding: ZIM's CFO said in the Q2 release (19 Aug 2026) that the expected H2 improvement 'would enable our Board of Directors to consider declaring a dividend to shareholders based on our third-quarter results'. The merger agreement restricts only SPECIAL dividends; regular dividends under the existing policy (about 30% of quarterly net income, 30-50% of annual) remain allowed, and the $0.88 Q4-2025 dividend was paid after signing. At the $4.77 consensus EPS (about $575m of net income, 120.6m shares) and net of the -$22m H1 loss, a ~30% payout is about $1.35-1.45 a share, about 4.7% of spot. On an arb name the dividend is value on top of the $35. A larger payout, at the high end of the policy or on a bigger Q3, adds; a board that withholds or trims it citing the merger agreement subtracts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on this line under the deal. ZIM skipped Q1 and Q2 2026 dividends because of the cumulative H1 loss. The $0.88 Q4-2025 dividend (paid 26 Mar 2026) was declared alongside the merger announcement, whose reaction was dominated by the deal premium.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the CFO flagged it three months ago, and arb holders model it. What the market cannot know is the board's choice of payout ratio, and whether it pays 30% of Q3 alone or of 9-month cumulative income. If the market priced a near-certain ~$1.4 plus a possible Q4 true-up before closing, the arb spread would be narrower than the $5.31 it is.
findings.independence: The restriction to special dividends only comes from ZIM's Q1 2026 release and the March dividend notice (https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/zim-reports-financial-results-for-the-first-quarter-of-2026/ ; https://www.itiger.com/news/2620445612). The CFO quote is repeated by TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/zim-stock-trades-at-30-below-hapag-lloyds-35-buyout-offer-its-payout-ratio-just-turned-negative). The payout size uses the same consensus as the reported-quarter finding.

findings.finding: The reported quarter is likely to land inside the range the 9 Oct guide already told the market to expect. H2 adjusted EBIT implied at $1.24-1.54bn, with Q2's ~$105m of finance and tax costs, puts Q3 EPS at roughly $4.3-6.2 depending on the Q3/Q4 split, which brackets consensus at $4.77 and leans slightly above it. Peers' Q3 freight rates were very strong (Hapag +23% q/q to $1,808/TEU; SCFI +46% q/q per Maersk), and ZIM is the most transpacific-levered of the three.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat EPS by a wide margin ($0.53-0.64 against an expected loss of about $0.29-0.33) and the stock fell 3.8% pre-market and 6% intraday (https://finviz.com/news/383708/zim-shares-fall-despite-strong-second-quarter-earnings-beat).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because the company pre-guided. The estimate spread ($3.85-5.15) shows that some stale numbers sit in the consensus, so the headline 'beat' or 'miss' depends on the aggregator. That moves the first minutes, not the close.
findings.independence: Hapag-Lloyd Q3 (https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/hapaglloyd-q3-2026-slides-earnings-surge-on-freight-rate-strength-93CH-5698915) and Maersk Q3 (https://www.foodbusinessmea.com/?p=2165405). The EPS bracket is my own arithmetic on ZIM's guide, not a sourced number.

findings.finding: Reaction function: on its last print under the deal (Q2 2026, 19 Aug 2026), ZIM beat EPS and revenue by a wide margin and issued a FY guide, then fell about 6% to $26.77. Peer Maersk raised its 2026 guide for the third time on 5 Nov 2026 and fell 8.6-11% because the raise was expected. ZIM goes into this print up 5.6% in five days, 3.9% below its 52-week high, and the option skew (though unreliable) pays for downside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The finding is itself the reaction history: -6% on the Q2 2026 beat, and the sector selling raises in November 2026 (Maersk).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a pattern, not a fact the market lacks. It matters because the 5-day run-up into the print (+5.64%, part of it after Hapag's 11 Nov raise) suggests holders positioned for good news. If the run-up were not a pre-positioning bid, the stock would not sit within 4% of its 52-week high on a capped cash deal.
findings.independence: Maersk's reaction (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/boxships/maersk-shares-fall-despite-third-profit-guidance-raise-in-2026) is a different company and event. ZIM's Q2 reaction is also covered by Finviz (https://finviz.com/news/383708/zim-shares-fall-despite-strong-second-quarter-earnings-beat).

findings.finding: Transpacific spot momentum has turned down into the print. Drewry's WCI composite fell three weeks running: $4,585 (22 Oct), $4,429, $4,389, then $4,305 (12 Nov), down 6.1%. Shanghai-LA was $7,416 (-1.6% on the week), and Drewry expects further transpacific declines, with blank sailings doubled to eight the following week. Any Q4/2027 commentary on the 08:00 ET call will be set against that trend, and the Maersk read was that 'congestion-driven rates fade'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Maersk fell 8.6-11% on 5 Nov 2026 despite a raise, with analysts citing rates expected to fade. ZIM fell on Q2 2026, with investors 'focused on the outlook for shipping conditions' (Finviz, 19 Aug 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: The WCI is public weekly, so this is mostly priced in level. What is unknown is how ZIM's management frames 2027 on the call. If the market expected a soft outlook, ZIM would not have run up 5.6% into the print.
findings.independence: This is the same Drewry series that the positive guidance finding reads for the Q4 level. Here the trend is used, there the level, and both can be true: Q4 averaging above the 9 Oct assumptions while still sliding. Maersk's caution is a different source (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/boxships/maersk-shares-fall-despite-third-profit-guidance-raise-in-2026).

findings.finding: Deal timeline has slipped and is unresolved. Israel's Government Companies Authority closed its review of the original structure on 29 Sep. A revised structure must clear the boards and start a fresh review. Hapag-Lloyd's CEO now targets closing in Q1 2027, not late 2026 (said at Hapag's Q3, 12 Nov). The outside date is February 2027, extendable to June 2027. A >10% shareholder group wants a new vote. ZIM's release and call on 18 Nov will likely restate its closing expectation (it said 'Q4 2026' in May and August) and may add news on the revised filing in either direction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean print-day history on deal commentary. The stock is at $29.69 against $35, an 18% spread that carries the deal risk.
findings.why_not_priced: The slip to Q1 2027 has been public since 12 Nov and is priced; the stock rose afterwards. Only a new fact on the call (revised application filed or accepted, or a second-vote requirement) would move it, and its sign is unknowable from here. Hence a near-zero centre with a wide band.
findings.independence: Hapag-Lloyd Q3 slides on the Q1 2027 timing (https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/hapaglloyd-q3-2026-slides-earnings-surge-on-freight-rate-strength-93CH-5698915); Forwarder News on the review clock (https://www.forwardernews.com/news/2026-10-14-hapag-lloyd-revises-zim-bid-terms).

outside_window.finding: Israeli GCA decision on the revised Hapag-Lloyd/FIMI structure (New ZIM with 16 vessels, scrutiny threshold at 10%). The merger outside date is February 2027, extendable to June 2027. This decides whether the $5.31 spread closes or the stock falls back toward standalone value.

Year-end true-up dividend (policy 30-50% of annual net income), declared with Q4 results around March 2027, if the deal has not closed by the record date. Potentially about $2-3 a share on FY net income of about $1bn or more.

searched_and_found_nothing: A November 2026 confirmation that the revised GCA application was actually filed or accepted: none found after the October reports
The merger agreement's exact interim-dividend covenant text: only the secondary 'special dividends restricted' language was found; the proxy and agreement exhibit were not reached
ZIM's own reaction history on prior prints beyond Q2 2026: the baseline is empty because SEC 6-K access was refused; only the Q2 2026 reaction was reconstructed from press
Any ZIM preview or analyst note expecting a second FY raise: none found

rejected_candidates.detail: A small network change already announced in September; immaterial to Q3 or the guide and folded into the general guidance read. The date was not verified from the document.

baseline_tension: The skew (+20.4, downside paid, but on an 81%-wide chain) and the 5-day run-up of +5.6% into a print the company largely pre-announced both argue for a sold or flat reaction. My positive items (a peer's second raise, the dividend) cut against that skew, so p_up sits at 49 rather than leaning long.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar: $3.85 / $4.77 / $5.15, no two agreeing; the quarter lands inside the 9 Oct guide): reported-quarter finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1; all sizes kept small

Rules 1 and 7 (the name sold its Q2 2026 beat; positive sign against a downside-paid skew): guidance finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8 and dividend finding from +0.5 to +0.4. The reaction-function finding stays at -1.0 and is not applied a second time
Rule 5 (peer and proxy transmission): Hapag and Drewry items kept, labelled as proxies in independence, not dropped
Scaled measurement: p_up moved from 52 to 49 and abs_move from 5.0 to 5.5 (the understatement lesson; Q2 2026 moved about 6% even under the deal cap)
